title.en: Word order: I often go to Keswick
title.sl: Besedni red: I often go to Keswick
title.it: L'ordine delle parole: I often go to Keswick
title.de: Die Wortstellung: I often go to Keswick

rule.en:
An English sentence keeps one order: **subject – verb – object**, then place and time: **Jack feeds the sheep in the morning.** The order stays the same when something else comes first: **In the morning Jack feeds the sheep.** (not *In the morning feeds Jack the sheep*). The order shows who does what, so the object can't move to the front.

The adjective goes before its noun and never changes: **the big fir tree**, **the big fir trees**, **a big tent**.

Words for how often (**always**, **often**, **usually**, **sometimes**, **never**) go before the main verb: **I often go to Keswick.** **Meg never barks.** But after **am / is / are**: **Jack is always happy.**

The object comes right after the verb, and words like very much come after it: **I like it very much.** (not *I like very much it*). Place comes before time: **We go to school every day.**

In questions the helping verb comes before the subject: **Do you like it?** **Is Jack happy?**
rule.sl:
Slovenski besedni red je prost, ker sklon pove, kdo kaj dela. Angleščina sklonov nima, zato ima stalen red: **osebek – glagol – predmet**, nato kraj in čas: **Jack feeds the sheep in the morning.** (Zjutraj Jack hrani ovce.) Predmeta ne moremo postaviti na začetek: *The sheep feed Jack* bi pomenilo, da ovce hranijo Jacka.

Pridevnik stoji pred samostalnikom in se nikoli ne spremeni: **the big fir tree**, **the big fir trees**, **a big tent** (velika jelka, velike jelke, velik šotor).

Besede, ki povedo, kako pogosto (**always**, **often**, **usually**, **sometimes**, **never**), stojijo pred glavnim glagolom: **I often go to Keswick.** (Pogosto grem v Keswick.) **Meg never barks.** Pri **am / is / are** pa stojijo za glagolom: **Jack is always happy.**

Predmet stoji takoj za glagolom, besede kot very much pa za predmetom: **I like it very much.** (Zelo mi je všeč; ne *I like very much it*). Kraj je pred časom: **We go to school every day.**

V vprašanju je pomožni glagol pred osebkom: **Do you like it?** **Is Jack happy?**
rule.it:
L'inglese tiene un ordine fisso: **soggetto – verbo – oggetto**, poi luogo e tempo: **Jack feeds the sheep in the morning.** (La mattina Jack dà da mangiare alle pecore.) L'oggetto non va all'inizio, e il soggetto non va dopo il verbo come in «arriva Jack»: **Jack is coming.**

L'aggettivo va prima del nome, al contrario dell'italiano, e non cambia mai: **the big fir tree**, **the big fir trees**, **a red apple** (una mela rossa), **red apples**.

Le parole di frequenza (**always**, **often**, **usually**, **sometimes**, **never**) vanno prima del verbo principale: **I often go to Keswick.** (Vado spesso a Keswick.) **Meg never barks.** Ma dopo **am / is / are**: **Jack is always happy.**

L'oggetto sta subito dopo il verbo, e very much va dopo l'oggetto: **I like it very much.** (Mi piace molto: in inglese ci vuole it; mai *I like very much it*). Il luogo va prima del tempo: **We go to school every day.**

Nelle domande l'ausiliare va prima del soggetto: **Do you like it?** **Is Jack happy?**
rule.de:
Das Englische hält immer eine Reihenfolge: **Subjekt – Verb – Objekt**, dann Ort und Zeit: **Jack feeds the sheep in the morning.** Anders als im Deutschen rückt das Verb nicht an die zweite Stelle, wenn etwas anderes vorn steht: **In the morning Jack feeds the sheep.** (Am Morgen füttert Jack die Schafe; nicht *In the morning feeds Jack*.) Und kein Verbteil wandert ans Ende: **I can swim very well.** (Ich kann sehr gut schwimmen.)

Das Adjektiv steht vor dem Nomen und hat nie eine Endung: **the big fir tree**, **the big fir trees**, **a big tent** (die große Tanne, die großen Tannen, ein großes Zelt).

Häufigkeitswörter (**always**, **often**, **usually**, **sometimes**, **never**) stehen vor dem Hauptverb: **I often go to Keswick.** (Ich fahre oft nach Keswick.) **Meg never barks.** Aber nach **am / is / are**: **Jack is always happy.**

Das Objekt steht direkt nach dem Verb, very much danach: **I like it very much.** (nicht *I like very much it*). Ort vor Zeit: **We go to school every day.**

In Fragen steht das Hilfsverb vor dem Subjekt: **Do you like it?** **Is Jack happy?**

examples.en: In the morning Jack feeds the sheep.
examples.it: La mattina Jack dà da mangiare alle pecore.
examples.de: Am Morgen füttert Jack die Schafe.

note.en: The time comes first, and still Jack feeds: subject, then verb.
note.sl: Čas je na začetku, a še vedno Jack feeds: osebek, nato glagol.
note.it: Il tempo è all'inizio, ma sempre Jack feeds: soggetto, poi verbo.
note.de: Die Zeit steht vorn, und trotzdem Jack feeds, nicht feeds Jack.

note.en: often goes before the main verb.
note.it: often va prima del verbo principale.

note.en: With is, always comes after it.
note.sl: Pri is stoji always za njim.

examples.en: Look at the big fir trees!
examples.de: Schau dir die großen Tannen an!

note.en: big stays big: the adjective never changes.
note.sl: big ostane big: pridevnik se ne spreminja.
note.it: big resta big: l'aggettivo non cambia mai.
note.de: big bleibt big: das Adjektiv ändert sich nie.

note.en: it right after like; very much at the end.
note.sl: it takoj za like, very much na koncu.
note.it: it subito dopo like, very much alla fine.
note.de: it direkt nach like, very much am Ende.

examples.en: Mrs Hartley reads us a story every Friday.
examples.sl: Gospa Hartley nam vsak petek prebere zgodbo.
examples.it: La signora Hartley ci legge una storia ogni venerdì.
examples.de: Frau Hartley liest uns jeden Freitag eine Geschichte vor.

examples.it: Meg non abbaia mai di notte.
